YES

The script verifies identical key sets and bit-exact equality of all 180 non-MLP tensors across the three checkpoints before writing anything, matches exactly the 64 MLP tensor names via `fullmatch`, computes each task vector against the unmodified `base` dict in float32 and casts back to the base dtype, copies all other tensors from base unchanged, and asserts `merged == 64` and `len(out) == 244` before saving to `out/T4/model.safetensors`.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
